question.explanation: Using the addition and the power rules, we get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(9e^x - 9x^2 + 11x - 20)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(9e^x) - \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(9x^2) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(11x) - \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(20) \\[5pt] & = 9\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(e^x) - 9\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(x^2) + 11\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(x) - 0 \\[5pt] & = 9e^x - 9(2x) + 11(1) \\[5pt] & = 9e^x - 18x + 11. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $f(x)=2\cdot 3^x$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.explanation:
Applying the formula, we get \begin{align*} f'(x)&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(2\cdot 3^x\right)\\[3pt] &= 2\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left( 3^x\right)\\[3pt] &= 2\ln 3\cdot 3^x . \end{align*}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is \begin{align*} \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &= \Big.2\ln 3\cdot 3^x\Big|_{x=1}\\[3pt] &=2\ln 3\cdot 3^{1}\\[3pt] &=2\ln 3\cdot 3\\[3pt] &=6\ln 3. \end{align*}

example.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Base Other Than e

question.text: Given that $f(x)=5^x + 2e^{x} -\ln{2}$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
question.explanation:
Applying the formula, we get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(5^x + 2e^{x} -\ln{2}\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(5^{x} \right)+ \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(2e^x\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(-\ln{2} \right) \\[5pt] & = 5^x \ln 5 + 2\dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(e^x\right) + 0 \\[5pt] & = 5^x \ln 5 +2e^x. \end{align}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is \begin{align*} \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=1} &= \Big.\left(5^x \ln 5 +2e^x\right)\Big|_{x=1}\\[3pt] &=5^1\cdot \ln 5+ 2\cdot e^1\\[3pt] &=5\ln{5} + 2e. \end{align*}
